identity.name: enrich_ravines
identity.description: Single-pass ENRICHER: spatial-joins parcels.geom against ravines (Spec 59 §8c) and writes the Chapter-658 flag + signed nearest-ravine distance + dataset lineage stamp in ONE set-based join UPDATE (#418 Layer-2), scoped to geom-bearing parcels whose lineage stamp is stale against the current ravines version. The pre-conversion #418 Layer-1 early-return (a cheap COUNT-only skip before opening any transaction) is RETIRED as a mechanism — the ENRICHER runner has no gated-skip branch by design — its OBSERVABLES are preserved: the Layer-2 scope predicate already yields a 0-row write in steady state, and parcels_ravine_enrich_skipped is re-derived from the scope count rather than a skip branch.

why_lock.text: Spec 59 L4b — 60, 'verified unassigned'; kept textually per Spec 122 §5.4 so the registry loop (src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts) stays green across the conversion.

guard_columns_why.text: The verbatim §8d triple guard (legacy ENRICH_SQL:179-181). The lineage stamp is INSIDE the guard — unlike geocode_permits' run-clock `geocoded_at` (source:"run_at", excluded from ITS guard by the LG-9 escape hatch), `ravine_dataset_version_when_enriched` here is source:"compute" — a content hash of the source dataset that stays CONSTANT across runs against the same ravines version, so including it in the guard is exactly what makes the second run write 0 rows rather than re-stamping every row on every run.

write_discipline.scope: p.geom IS NOT NULL AND p.ravine_dataset_version_when_enriched IS DISTINCT FROM $1

invalidates.when: load-parcels.js's ON CONFLICT nulls the stamp via a CASE gated ONLY on parcels.geometry::jsonb IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.geometry::jsonb (#418 DEC-FENCE2, locked by src/tests/db/load-parcels-ravine-invalidation.db.test.ts) — app code, NOT migration 242's trigger, which deliberately covers only massing/zoning (mig 242 header). A load_ravines source_dataset_version bump stales every parcel through the SAME scope predicate this step's own write_discipline.scope declares.

why.text: Exactly one write statement per invocation, in every mode and on every chain — the #418 Layer-2 WITH...UPDATE, executed through ctx.joinUpdate. There is no batching and no full/incremental split beyond the scope predicate itself (staleness.mode_select "none").

staleness.scope: parcels whose geom IS NOT NULL AND ravine_dataset_version_when_enriched IS DISTINCT FROM the producer's (load_ravines) most recent completed source_dataset_version

why.text: The ST_Intersects boolean join and the geography KNN nearest-ravine distance are non-viable without PostGIS. Ported verbatim from the legacy assertPreconditions (DEC-F, §3.10) — there is no non-PostGIS fallback path to retire.
Migration 039. Without it the materialized parcel_c centroid CTE's own join back to parcels (and every other GIST-dependent step sharing this index) degrades to a sequential scan over 486,530 rows.
Planar GIST (migration 167) — binds the ST_Intersects boolean-membership join. Without it every parcel seq-scans all ~854 ravines for the boolean half alone (DeepSeek HIGH, pre-conversion review).

Geography GIST (migration 167) — binds the `pc.cg <-> r.geom::geography` KNN operator that the LATERAL nearest-ravine distance join depends on. This is the index the Spec 59 §11.1 inline-centroid form (review_followups #413) fails to bind, producing the measured ~2h/0-rows-progress pathology this compute's materialized-centroid rewrite exists to avoid.
DEC-E — migration 168. A missing column would otherwise surface as a cryptic 42703 from the write's own IS DISTINCT FROM scope predicate rather than a named refusal.

on_check_error_why.text: Every declared check reads a count the library already measured in the same run (the coverage/counts SQL in computePostPhase); a check that throws is a compute defect, not an upstream data condition, and must redden the run rather than silently drop its row (the geocode_permits / compute_centroids precedent).

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE is_in_ravine_protection_area AND ravine_distance_m > 0

why.text: L2's whole sign semantic, both directions locked separately (F-RC1b): a parcel flagged in-ravine must carry a NON-POSITIVE distance (0 inside/intersecting, negative deeper in). A `CASE WHEN ... THEN -1` port error breaks this silently while leaving every other check green — this is the ONLY row that would notice. MEASURED 0 across all 486,530 parcels, 2026-09-18.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE NOT is_in_ravine_protection_area AND ravine_distance_m < 0

why.text: The inverse direction of the same sign semantic (F-RC1b): a parcel NOT flagged in-ravine must never carry a negative distance. MEASURED 0 across all 486,530 parcels, 2026-09-18.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int FROM parcels WHERE is_in_ravine_protection_area AND ravine_distance_m IS NULL

why.text: F-RC1b, third direction: the boolean and the distance are written by the SAME statement from the SAME LATERAL join, so a flagged parcel with a NULL distance is evidence the two columns were set by different runs/paths, not evidence of a degenerate geometry (a degenerate geometry instead shows up as parcels_invalid_geom_count with in_ravine=false, since a NULL centroid never joins to any ravine). MEASURED 0 across all 486,530 parcels, 2026-09-18.

plausibility.sql: SELECT (-1 * MIN(ravine_distance_m))::float FROM parcels WHERE ravine_distance_m IS NOT NULL
plausibility.retighten_when: never — this is a PHYSICAL bound (Toronto's ravine network + parcel fabric), not a convergence target, mirroring geocode_permits' Toronto-bbox plausibility row. If the observed magnitude ever exceeds this ceiling the response is to find the parcel/ravine geometry that produced it, not to widen the bound. Measured live: the most-negative distance is -1470.30 m (magnitude 1470.30), against a declared ceiling of 2000 m, so the bound is currently vacuous and declared anyway — its value is in the CLASS of failure it catches (a mis-signed distance, or a unit/CRS error), not in a value expected to move.

why.text: F-RC1a — Reality-Check plan-altitude demand: a bound on how far a parcel can sit "inside" the deepest ravine (the magnitude of the most-negative ravine_distance_m), city-invariant, seeded with generous headroom above the measured live magnitude (1470.30 m, measured 2026-09-18). MEASURED, LIVE DEFECT AVOIDED: verdict.js's LIMIT_NUMBER_RE (a digits-only pattern, no sign) mangles a NEGATIVE `limit_from_config`-resolved value into a double-negative string ("value_min --2000", reproduced live 2026-09-18 running this exact check against the local DB before this fix) — a pre-existing library gap, out of this conversion's authorized scope (Ask A2 is the ONE sanctioned runner change). The SQL is negated instead so the compared value and its config-resolved bound are both POSITIVE, sidestepping the defect entirely rather than patching shared verdict.js code. Filed in review_followups.md as a library defect for LIMIT_NUMBER_RE to eventually admit a leading sign.

plausibility.sql: SELECT MAX(ravine_distance_m)::float FROM parcels WHERE ravine_distance_m IS NOT NULL
plausibility.retighten_when: never — the mirror-image ceiling bound of ravine_distance_m_min_observed, same physical-bound reasoning. Measured live maximum 2739.69 m against a declared ceiling of 20000 m.

why.text: F-RC1a, ceiling half. Externalized as its own logic variable (enrich_ravines_distance_plausible_max_m) for the same reason as the floor.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT ravine_dataset_version_when_enriched)::int FROM parcels WHERE ravine_dataset_version_when_enriched IS NOT NULL
plausibility.retighten_when: never — this is an INFO visibility row, not a pass/fail gate. A converged fleet reads exactly 1; a value > 1 is not itself a defect (it is the expected transient state mid-recompute, immediately after a load_ravines version bump and before every stale parcel has been re-touched) but it is otherwise invisible anywhere else in this step's audit table, which is the whole point of F-RC1c.

why.text: F-RC1c — an INFO row counting distinct non-null lineage stamps, so a multi-stamp partial-convergence state (some parcels re-touched against a new ravines version, others still carrying the old one) is VISIBLE in the audit table rather than only inferable by cross-referencing pipeline_runs. Measured 2026-09-18: 1 distinct value, matching the newest completed load_ravines run's own source_dataset_version.

plausibility.sql: SELECT MAX(ravine_distance_m)::float FROM parcels WHERE ravine_distance_m IS NOT NULL
plausibility.retighten_when: never — a PHYSICAL bound, the mirror-image concern of ravine_distance_m_max_observed/_min_magnitude_observed (both value_max ceilings, which a degrees-not-metres collapse would satisfy trivially — every distance shrinking toward ~0.03 stays comfortably under either ceiling and neither would ever fire). This row catches EXACTLY that regression class: the observed MAXIMUM distance must clear a floor (100 m) far below the measured live value (2,739.69 m) but far above what a degrees-scale collapse would produce, so a unit/CRS regression that silently shrinks every distance is caught by the ONE direction the two ceiling checks cannot see.

why.text: Output-panel O4 (Reality-Check, 2026-09-18): both existing distance checks are value_max ceilings; a degrees-not-metres regression collapses every distance toward ~0.03 and would PASS both silently. Added as a floor check on the observed MAXIMUM (not the minimum magnitude, which a collapse would also shrink toward 0 and satisfy just as trivially as the ceilings) — the schema's bound grammar admits value_min (step.schema.json definitions.bound, verified against src/tests/step-library.logic.test.ts's own verdictLib.evaluateLimit('value_min ...') proof), so no schema change is needed. Externalized as its own logic variable per Rule 3, seeded at 100 (min 0, max 1000) — comfortably below the measured 2,739.69 m and comfortably above a plausible degrees-scale collapse band.

limitations.what: RV-L3 — the pre-conversion invalid-geometry ratio guard (throw when producer invalid_geometry_skipped/feature_count > 5%) is NOT externalized as a logic variable, despite the batch-2 plan's own tunables census (§2 var #3) proposing one. Measured 2026-09-18: `execution.enrich_hooks.contract_read` is resolved and CALLED by the runner as `hookFn(pool)` ONLY (scripts/lib/step/index.js:3089, and identically for enrich_parcels' readZoningContract) — no `config` argument reaches a contract_read hook today. Threading it through would be a SECOND runner change beyond Ask A2's authorized one-line `passCtx.contract` addition. The ratio therefore stays the pinned pre-conversion literal (0.05) inside scripts/lib/compute/enrich-ravines.js rather than being declared as a logic variable no code path could ever read (Rule 12: 'a declared guard that cannot arm is a violation'). Filed as a followup for whichever WF next threads config into enrich_hooks.contract_read generally.
limitations.measured: scripts/lib/step/index.js:3086-3093 (contractHook resolved and called with (pool) only) vs scripts/lib/compute/enrich-parcels.js readZoningContract(pool) (same one-arg signature), 2026-09-18.

limitations.what: RV-L2 — guards.srid and guards.empty_source are DECLARATIVE, not runner-enforced preconditions. Measured 2026-09-18: scripts/lib/step/index.js has zero references to either field; both are read by COMPUTE modules directly where a step needs the value (the link-massing.js / link-neighbourhoods.js precedent for guards.srid) or are structurally unused (guards.empty_source has no generic runner consumer at all — link-massing's own empty_source_guard check function is what actually enforces it, and even that is a non-halting WARN/FAIL row, not a HALT). Because the legacy L14 behaviour genuinely HALTS (throws) rather than reports, the real enforcement of L14 (ravines must be non-empty) and the SRID=4326 assertion is folded into the contract_read hook (readRavineContract), which is guaranteed to run pre-transaction on every invocation — NOT into guards.srid/guards.empty_source, which are declared here for documentation/convention parity with the rest of the fleet only.

recovery.reset: No TRUNCATE/rebuild mechanism and none is needed — a plain re-run re-evaluates every geom-bearing parcel whose stamp disagrees with the current ravines version (staleness.scope) and the IS DISTINCT FROM triple guard makes an unnecessary re-stamp cheap. Nulling parcels.ravine_dataset_version_when_enriched by hand for a scoped set of parcels IS a valid targeted reset — it re-admits exactly those rows to the next run's scope predicate.

interrupted_why.text: The single write target sits inside ONE shared transaction (execution.txn_scope "step", the phase's own txn "shared"), so a run killed mid-statement leaves parcels exactly as it found them — there is no half-written state, the same guarantee geocode_permits' identical posture rests on. force_full_on_next_run is still the ACCURATE declaration and not a concession: runEnrichPhase folds staleness.detectInterruptedRetraction into the full/incremental decision before any pass runs (reachable), and because this step's scope predicate re-admits every stale parcel unconditionally on every run (staleness.scope is a lineage predicate evaluated fresh each time, not a one-shot flag), "the next run does a full pass over whatever is still stale" is a promise this step keeps whether or not the prior run was interrupted (accurate).

before_image_why.text: recovery.before_image applies to a retraction (outputs.writes[].retract != 'none'); this step's sole write target declares retract:"none" — it only ever stamps a value, never clears one to NULL.

why.text: A4 ruling (operator, 2026-09-18): declares the scanned population, following the enrich_parcels ENRICHER precedent (matched.compute.total_parcels_scanned) rather than preserving the legacy's records_total:null. DECLARE THE ROOT THAT RESOLVES: the runner resolves counters.<slot>.source against {matched, written, records_meta} — matched.compute.<name> resolves while a bare compute.* resolves NULL for every ENRICHER (enrich_parcels' own three counters read null since conversion for exactly this reason, filed HIGH 2026-09-16).

This step INSERTs nothing — the sole write target is an UPDATE, and class N's own executor structurally refuses any statement text containing INSERT INTO or ON CONFLICT (JOIN_UPDATE_FORBIDDEN_RE, scripts/lib/step/write.js), so the 0 is enforced rather than merely expected. Declared as a finite literal 0 rather than omitted, because an omitted source resolves null and null reads as "not counted" (Spec 48 §3.6).
COUNTER-ROOT (fast invariant #26): write.targetKey(0) returns "e1" (scripts/lib/step/write.js:158) — the rowCount of the sole declared write target, one-to-one with the legacy's `updated` counter.
